prompts.note: D1: <<\EOF is a quoted delimiter, so the body is literal and the sed -i inside it never runs.
D3: an indented EOF does not end a plain heredoc; the body is expanded by bash, so the sed -i in it writes src/a.ts. No check follows.
D1: the apostrophe in a <<\EOF body is literal and does not hide the later echo $(sed -i ... src/b.ts), a real write.
D2: a heredoc nested in a substitution of an unquoted heredoc body is not followed; the command is opaque but no edit is resolved, so no-changes.
